All four cases pass. Here is a summary of every change:

**`HashMap.java`**

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| `private final int initialCapacity` | New field; stores the capacity passed at construction time |
| `private static final int DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 20` | Replaces the magic literal `20` that appeared in multiple places |
| `HashMap(int initialCapacity, ProbingStrategy)` | New primary constructor; all others delegate to it |
| `HashMap(int initialCapacity)` | New convenience constructor; delegates with `LinearProbingStrategy` |
| `HashMap(ProbingStrategy)` | Now delegates to the primary constructor with `DEFAULT_CAPACITY` |
| `HashMap()` | Now delegates to the primary constructor with `DEFAULT_CAPACITY` and `LinearProbingStrategy` |
| `clear()` | Resets `capacity` to `initialCapacity` instead of the hardcoded `20`; `resize()` is unchanged — it always doubles the *current* `capacity`, so the growth sequence naturally starts from whatever `initialCapacity` was |
